findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment:
(i) THIS IS A SECOND REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed a cutting board stored behind the faucet of the triple sink, where it could be contaminated by food debris or water splashes. CORRECTED: PIC moved the cutting board up above onto the drying rack during the inspection. Ensure that cutting boards are always stored in a position that does not pose the risk of contamination.
(ii) Observed that the baffles inside the ice machine contained a buildup of soil residues. PIC and inspector discussed the establishment’s regular cleaning schedule, but found that the baffles had not been on the cleaning schedule. Inspector will Follow Up with the establishment to confirm that the ice machine baffles have been cleaned to sight and touch. Ensure that all equipment food-contact surfaces are clean to sight and touch.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

findings.title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
findings.comment: Observed that the establishment does not currently have a probe style thermometer. PIC will have a new probe style thermometer in the establishment by the Follow Up date, and will contact the Inspector when the thermometer has arrived. Ensure that all food temperature measuring device is provided and available for use to maintain food temperatures.
findings.citation_text: 4-302.12 Food Temperature Measuring Devices. (A) FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall be provided and readily accessible for use in ensuring attainment and maintenance of FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3. (B) A TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE with a suitable small-diameter probe that is designed to measure the temperature of thin masses shall be provided and readily accessible to accurately measure the temperature in thin FOODS such as MEAT patties and FISH filets. [Pf]

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.comment:
THIS IS A FIRST REPEAT VIOLATION. Observed the reach-in freezer in the ware washing room has an accumulation of frost. The inspector and PIC discussed unplugging the freezer for a complete defrost. Ensure that the reach-in freezer is a smooth, easily cleanable surface by the next routine inspection. 

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition. [C]

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment:
Observed the following non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned: 
(i) THIS IS A THIRD REPEAT VIOLATION. The grease accumulation around the fryer. The accumulation is on the floor and sides and on the pipes above the fryer. The grease above the fryer could potentially drip onto food cooking below.
(ii) THIS IS A FIRST REPEAT VIOLATION: The dust accumulation behind and underneath the soda machine in the kitchen.
Ensure that the above referenced non-food contact surfaces are cleaned to sight and touch by the next routine inspection.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment: Observed foods in the clear door sliding cooler had internal temperatures above 41F. The following temperatures were recorded with a probe thermometer: humus 48F, humus cups 50F, feta-cheese spinach pie 49F, cut leafy greens 54F, gyro sauce (sour cream base) 54F, feta cheese 51F, kasseri cheese 51F, and mozzarella cheese 51F. There were hamburger patties that had an internal temperature of 44F that were immediately moved into another cooler. All foods had been inside the cooler since at least 11am this morning (some of the foods had been inside the cooler overnight) meaning the 4 hour time-as-control window had passed when the foods were discarded after 3pm. All temperature control for safety (TCS) foods (other than the hamburger patties) were discarded during the inspection. Non-TCS foods were allowed to remain in the cooler (such as non-TCS vegetables and sauces). The PIC will be scheduling service for the cooler. Until the cooler is serviced and functioning properly the cooler will not be used to store TCS foods. The inspector will follow-up on 5/30/2025 to ensure that the sliding cooler is functioning properly.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored.
findings.comment: THIS IS A FIRST REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed the feta cheese scoop in the prep cooler was stored with the handle in contact with the feta. After a conversation with the inspector the PIC switched the feta scoop with another scoop that has a longer handle to facilitate proper storage. Ensure that handles for ready-to-eat foods are always stored above food to avoid contamination.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
Observed a scoop being stored with the handle in contact with feta cheese in the prep cooler. The inspector educated that handles cannot touch ready-to-eat foods. The handle was moved into a position where it did not touch the feta cheese during the inspection. Ensure that food is always protected from cross contamination during storage. 

3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Observed a cutting board stored behind the faucet of the triple sink. The inspector discussed with the PIC who removed the cutting board to be cleaned. The PIC was instructed to store the clean cutting board in a position that does not pose a risk of contamination. Ensure that food contact surfaces are always clean to sight and touch. 

4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION. Observed the fryer and surrounding area (including, but not limited to, the sides and lower area) are in need of cleaning. Non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of soil residues. Ensure the fryer and surrounding area are cleaned by the next routine inspection. 

4-601.11: (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Observed the container storing the ice scoop was soiled with debris. The container was removed from service and washed during the inspection. Non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of soil residues. Ensure that the container storing the ice scoop is cleaned on a regular basis. 

4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.
